notes.title: The Mighty 8th VR Dev Blog 3 – The Briefing Room
notes.content:
Welcome to the third Dev Blog for “The Mighty 8th VR”.

In this blog we will be sharing developments on The Briefing Room, The Officers Club, Terrain, and a little bit more about our vision and what we are working on in the background.
[previewyoutube=6dCShMFACeo;full][/previewyoutube]
0:00 [url=https://youtu.be/6dCShMFACeo?si=d-_AxonKc5DbnE02]Briefing Room[/url]
1:03 [url=https://youtu.be/6dCShMFACeo?si=fsT_guYXJ0K_lt2t&t=63]Officer’s Club[/url]
2:12 [url=https://youtu.be/6dCShMFACeo?si=VWpjh9lQAJXmMS9w&t=132]Airfield[/url]
3:58 [url=https://youtu.be/6dCShMFACeo?si=OwQQ5C1G8aAN19nF&t=237]Terrain[/url]

[h2]The Briefing Room and Officers Club[/h2]
Currently we have taken some liberties and attached the Briefing Room to the Officer's Club at the end of a hall. This has been done to keep the idea of our virtual lobby together in one place without the need to traverse between areas and juggle scene loads when doing so.  However, this may change during development.

Our main goal is to create an immersive space where crews can actively plan out their roles and communicate amongst each other prior to deployment.  


[h2]Terrain[/h2]
Our environmental artists have been busy working on improvements to the airfield and the surrounding terrain. The video above shows the kind of detail we are currently achieving, and we can’t wait to show you some of your planned targets in future development updates. 

You will note roads, bodies of water and other features that will act as frames of reference for your navigator as your crew heads toward the target and back to the airfield.

[h2]Full Body IK work is in Progress[/h2]
We will share this in future dev blogs but one of our goals to keep you and your crew feeling immersed is to ensure we can show the full body and have that act correctly in different situations. We looked at the idea of just doing hands and heads like you see in some VR experiences, but we feel that may break immersion in this case.

[h2]Flight Gear[/h2]
The art team has been busy preparing some of the gear for the crew, and we are happy to share some of the work in progress below.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121703/32e1ed2e5810f69891d48066d3b540b31091e794.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121703/b6fc961130d7564c5c439a7b7b91db1c58610e12.png[/img]

Thanks for taking the time to read this far and we look forward to sharing more with you in the future.

notes.title: The Mighty 8th VR Dev Blog 2 - Test Flight
notes.content:
Welcome to the second of our Dev Blog series for “The Mighty 8th VR”.

Today we are happy to share with you our further work in progress. 

[h2]Test Flight[/h2]

[previewyoutube=dSXVbhOnUiI;full][/previewyoutube]

We have aimed to create a sandbox and training areas around the Thorpe Abbotts airbase so players can test their skills and get some familiarity with guns prior to taking to the sky.

You will notice in the video that the airfield is starting to come to life. There are many vehicles moving from place to place and beyond. The keen-eyed among you will also notice a G506 driving around with a very interesting gun mounted on the back, whilst we don’t show you how this works in today's video it will come in videos further down the track.

The video also shows work in progress of some of the various roles that we have been implementing and testing. You will notice multiple gunner roles, pilot and bombardier roles are starting to take shape. Whilst we have been working on the Norden Bomb Sight, we felt it was better for us to save that for a future video. 

[h3]VR Notes:[/h3]
The video has been captured on a Steam PCVR build on an Oculus Quest 2 connected via wifi using Virtual Desktop. The game will also work via the Steam app and Oculus Airlink, using motion controllers. We have also been testing with hand tracking on the Quest 2, and that is partially working already.  We aim to support as many headsets as possible when the game launches.

[h3]Thanks for your support[/h3]
Thanks again for your support so far. The team is making great strides now as we have overcome some real technical hurdles we faced early on. We look forward to sharing more with you soon. 

Please feel free to reach out with comments and questions and we will see if we can cover them in future blogs. 

We are also avid VR gamers here, so if you have played an amazing VR game recently that you think our team should check out feel free to name-drop it in the comments.
